flashcards.definition: Main metabolic cell body of neurone containing nucleus, organelles, and Nissl's granules.
Clumps of Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free ribosomes synthesizing protein in cyton and dendrites; ABSENT in axon.
Conical region connecting cyton to axon; lacks Nissl's granules; site of action potential initiation.
Uninsulated gaps in axon myelin sheath rich in voltage-gated Na+ channels enabling saltatory impulse conduction.
Fast leaping action potential propagation from node to node along myelinated axons up to 120 m/s.
Star-shaped glial cells forming Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) perivascular end-feet and maintaining ionic homeostasis.
Glial cells forming myelin sheath around multiple axons inside the Central Nervous System.
Small phagocytic macrophage neuroglia defending CNS tissue against infection and clearing debris.
Ciliated epithelial-like cells lining brain ventricles and central spinal canal; circulate Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF).
PNS neuroglial cells wrapping around peripheral axons to synthesize myelin sheath.
Mature human neurones lack active centrioles and cannot divide post-birth.
Presynaptic Ca2+ influx causes neurotransmitter exocytosis into synaptic cleft, binding postsynaptic receptors.
